title: Sell-through and distributor history upload readiness (2 years: Amazon, Takealot, Pinnacle)
acceptance_criteria: Monday-Sunday is the tenant default week calendar for every customer and distributor; a per-customer override stays possible.
A history line with a full sale date loads at day grain and rolls up into Monday-Sunday weeks for weekly views.
A file that carries only week numbers does not apply until the uploader confirms the year at upload (pre-filled from the file name or folder). The year is never guessed.

A newer load replaces only the figures it carries: units sold, on-hand, in-transit and on-order are superseded independently. A stock-only file never wipes sales; a sales-only file never wipes stock. Superseded figures are kept with the superseding load; nothing is hard-deleted. Refines D-0090; cross-grain supersession stays.
A week with no reported on-hand does not break the stock chain: the chain restarts at the next reported on-hand and the gap tab names that week 'no on-hand reported'.
Built for customer sell-through (Amazon, Takealot). Pinnacle on the distributor sales/inventory path gets the same rules where it has the same gap; differences are listed.

Clone proof: a synthetic 2-year set per source (day-dated lines, a week-number-only file with a confirmed year, sales-only and stock-only files for one week, a re-upload, an overlapping correction) prints per-customer units and on-hand before / after / after re-running the whole set; the re-run changes nothing. No writes to cip except migrations after their clone proof.
Test and fixture data is out of scope.
Full API pytest and full web vitest green on cip_test.
